summary.text: An ester is a compound derived from an acid in which the hydrogen of at least one acidic hydroxyl group is replaced by an organyl group.
One way to form an ester is a substitution reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol.
Esters often smell pleasant and are used as fragrances, solvents, plastics (polyesters) and lubricants.

facts.label: Fats and oils
facts.value: Glycerides are fatty acid esters of glycerol

facts.label: Biology link
facts.value: Esters of phosphoric acid form DNA's backbone

items.prompt: A chemist mixes a carboxylic acid with an alcohol and gets a substitution reaction. What kind of compound forms?

options.label: An ester
An ether
An amide
A ketone

items.explain: The substitution reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol forms an ester.

items.prompt: Butter and celery owe part of their aroma to lactones. What kind of molecule is a lactone?

options.label: A chain-shaped alcohol
A salt of a fatty acid
A form of glycerol
A cyclic carboxylic ester

items.explain: Lactones are cyclic carboxylic esters and contribute to the aroma of fruits, butter, cheese and celery.

items.prompt: Compared with the corresponding amides, how are carboxylic acid esters expected to behave?

options.label: Lower melting and lower boiling points
Higher melting and higher boiling points
Higher melting but lower boiling points
The same melting and boiling points

items.explain: Esters tend to be less rigid (lower melting point) and more volatile (lower boiling point) than the corresponding amides.

items.prompt: Most of the fat in a cooking oil is made of which kind of compound?

options.label: Salts of fatty acids and sodium
Amides of fatty acids and glycerol
Fatty acid esters of glycerol
Plain hydrocarbons with no oxygen

items.explain: Glycerides are fatty acid esters of glycerol and make up the bulk of animal fats and vegetable oils.

items.prompt: An ester called butyl acetate is made from butanol and acetic acid. What does that name show?

options.label: It is built from the name of the alcohol alone
It is built from the names of the parent alcohol and the parent acid
It is built from a random trivial label with no link
It is built from the acid alone, plus a count of carbons

items.explain: Ester names derive from the parent alcohol and the parent acid, as with butyl acetate from butanol and acetic acid.

items.prompt: Compared with an alcohol of similar size, how polar is an ester?

options.label: More polar than the alcohol
Exactly as polar as the alcohol
Less polar than the alcohol
Not polar at all

items.explain: Esters derived from carboxylic acids and alcohols are more polar than ethers but less polar than alcohols.
